Upon arrival, I checked in with the store manager, who reported seeing a mouse running around in the back of the store. I immediately performed a thorough inspection of the designated back area, paying close attention to corners, baseboards, and behind equipment. During this inspection, I found no active signs of rodent activity, such as fresh droppings, nesting materials, or rub marks. To prevent any future entry, I identified several potential access points and sealed them completely using steel wool. Specifically, I sealed a small hole in the tile flooring surrounding a white electrical cable penetration. I also packed a gap leading into an open section of a floor drain grate to prevent pests from traveling up through the line. Additionally, I sealed a tight gap found behind a structural junction against the wall paneling, and securely stuffed the open space surrounding a black utility pipe where it penetrates through the textured wall. As a proactive monitoring and trapping measure, I successfully installed two Tin Cat multi-catch mouse traps in strategic locations throughout the back area. I will check these devices during our next scheduled service to monitor for any activity and ensure the perimeter remains secure.

Upon arrival, I checked in with store manager Juliana, who reported recent sightings of flying insects throughout the retail space. I initiated a comprehensive inspection of the facility, beginning with all rodent monitoring stations. A thorough check of all "Tin Cat" live-catch traps revealed zero activity, indicating that current rodent exclusion and baiting measures remain fully effective. Shifting focus to the flying insect issue, my inspection of the trash room revealed a localized population of small flies breeding near the waste receptacles. To address this and prevent further spread, I treated the entire trash room with Alpine WSG, a highly effective residual insecticide. As a proactive preventative measure, I also applied Alpine WSG along all baseboards throughout the back area of the store to create a protective barrier. Given the seasonal pressure and the presence of these flying pests, the current control measures need reinforcement. I highly recommend the immediate installation of at least two additional insect light traps (fly lights) in key transition zones to effectively intercept and monitor fly activity moving forward
